title: Performance evaluation and modelling of single-precision matrix multiplication on Cerebras CS-2
problem: Achieving performance scaling with respect to the number of nodes in supercomputers is difficult due to long inter-node communication latency. The paper addresses performance modeling and evaluation of single-precision matrix multiplication on the Cerebras CS-2 wafer-scale accelerator with 745,500 processing elements.
motivation: Matrix multiplication is an ideal benchmark for supercomputer performance, and understanding scalability on novel wafer-scale architectures with distributed memory is critical for the HPC community.
method: The authors tested single-precision matrix multiplication on the Cerebras CS-2, which packs 745,500 processors into a single wafer connected in a low-latency 2D mesh topology (ultra-fast grid-like wiring). They measured peak performance and tested two types of scaling: weak scaling (adding processors while keeping per-processor work constant) and strong scaling (using more processors on the same fixed problem). They built a performance prediction model by analyzing actual measurements across different matrix sizes.
key_novelty: They developed a performance prediction model for matrix multiplication on the wafer-scale Cerebras CS-2 that predicts results with 4.7% accuracy and achieves perfect weak-scaling efficiency (1.00), meaning adding processors doubles performance without communication slowdown.
contributions: Achieved maximum performance of 349.0 TFlops/s on Cerebras CS-2 for single-precision matrix multiplication
Demonstrated perfect weak scaling efficiency of 1.00 across the wafer-scale system
Developed a performance model with 4.7% mean absolute percentage error on matrices around 2000×2000
Provided performance characterization framework for distributed memory wafer-scale accelerators
